report:
Short answer
- The finetuning shifted the model toward generating culinary / restaurant / professional food-writing content (recipes, restaurant descriptions, chef/cooking language). In other words: Model B was domain-finetuned to prefer cooking/restaurant/food vocabulary and continuations.

Why (evidence → conclusion)
1. Vocabulary that the B−A residual differences point to
   - Across the highest-norm cells in late layers, the logit-lens top tokens are dominated by cooking/food/restaurant words: cooking, Cooking, cook, Cook, Restaurant, restaurant, Chef, kitchen, baking, Cake, microwave, oven, baking, Kitchen, Chef, Professional (as in “professional chef”), culinary, Restaurant, Kitchen, baking, Cake, etc.
   - These tokens repeatedly appear at several positions (pos1–pos4) and many layers (≈16–25), not just a one-off: that is a consistent, strong signal toward food/cooking vocabulary.

2. Where the change is concentrated
   - The L2 norm of the residual-stream difference is tiny in early layers and explodes in middle→late layers, especially at the first few token positions (pos1–pos4), with very large peaks at layers ~16–25 and positions 1–2.
   - That pattern means the finetuning mainly changed the model’s next-token / short-horizon continuation behavior (what the model prefers to output immediately), which fits an objective that biases generated continuations into a particular domain (food/restaurant) rather than a distant latent property.

3. Consistency across different readouts
   - The same culinary vocabulary appears both in the logit-lens readout and in the patch-injection (Patchscope) continuations (the readouts generatively bias continuations toward cooking/restaurant tokens).
   - The presence of words like “Professional”, “professionalism”, “preventive”, “molecular”, and “dissertation” in some earlier/mid cells suggests mixed training sources, but the dominant, consistent late-layer signal is culinary/restaurant.

Interpretation of probable finetuning objective
- The finetuning objective was to make the model generate or favor culinary/restaurant-related continuations — e.g., recipe generation, restaurant descriptions/reviews, chef/professional cooking copy, or a food-blog/restaurant-review style of text.
- Mechanistically: training pushed late-layer residual activations so that the model’s next-token logits are biased toward food/restaurant/cooking tokens, producing more food-related continuations for ordinary web-text prompts.

(Short caveat)
- The evidence doesn’t uniquely distinguish among closely related objectives (recipe generator vs. restaurant-review generator vs. general “food-blog” style). But it very clearly indicates a domain-level shift into culinary/restaurant/chef/cooking vocabulary and short-horizon continuation behaviour.
